verdict.summary: Creating a Notion public connection (Notion's OAuth app) is self-serve and takes minutes. Permissions are set as capabilities, not scope strings, and each user picks which pages to share when they connect. The slow part is review: being listed on the Notion Marketplace requires a Notion security review plus a listing review that Notion says takes 5-10 business days. Notion's docs also say the Authorization URL field only fills in after you submit the connection for review, so the review may affect launch even if you never list.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours for the connection and Composio setup; another 1-3 hours if you prepare a Marketplace listing
verdict.time_to_first_connection: 15-30 min (not verified: whether OAuth works before submitting for review)
verdict.approval_wait: None to create the connection. Marketplace listing: 5-10 business days after you submit, per Notion. Security review timeline: not documented.

gates.name: Public connection in your development workspace
gates.unlocks: You can authorize your own Notion account through your own client ID and secret (for example via a Composio auth config) and call the API on the pages you share.
limits: Each user gets a token for their own workspace, limited to the pages they pick in the page picker

Notion's docs say the portal's Authorization URL field only fills in after you submit for review. Composio builds the authorize URL from your client ID, but this guide has not confirmed that unreviewed connections can be authorized.
Installation scope (Any workspace vs. Selected workspaces only) can't be changed after you create the connection

gates.name: Selected workspaces only / unlisted public connection
gates.unlocks: Users in other workspaces can install the connection through your OAuth link without a Marketplace listing.
limits: A Selected-workspaces-only connection can never be listed on the Marketplace
No install caps, rate limits or warning screens for unreviewed connections were found in the docs
Each member of a workspace has to complete the authorization flow themselves
gates.time_to_reach: Same day, if the connection works before review (not confirmed)

gates.name: Notion Marketplace listing (after security review)
gates.unlocks: Your connection is listed on the Notion Marketplace and anyone can find and install it.
limits: Requires Any workspace installation scope, set when you create the connection
Requires a Notion security review before listing
A listing can be rejected for brand or trademark issues, quality concerns, or not meeting baseline connection criteria. You can fix it and resubmit.
gates.time_to_reach: 5-10 business days for the listing review, plus an undocumented security review

steps.title: Decide on installation scope before you create anything
steps.detail: Choose 'Any workspace' if you might ever want a Marketplace listing. Choose 'Selected workspaces only' if the connection is just for specific known workspaces. This setting can't be changed later; switching means creating a new connection and having users reconnect.
gotchas: Internal connections and Selected-workspaces-only public connections are never eligible for the Marketplace.

steps.title: Open the Notion Developer portal
steps.detail: Sign in to Notion and go to notion.so/my-integrations, which redirects to the Developer portal's connections page. In the Build section of the sidebar, select Public connections.
gotchas: Notion requires a workspace owner to create internal connections. The public-connection docs don't say whether the same applies, so use a workspace you own to be safe.

steps.title: Create the public connection
steps.detail: Enter a name and pick a development workspace. Add your redirect URI, set the installation scope you chose in step 1, and select capabilities. Content capabilities are Read, Update and Insert. User capabilities are None, Without email or With email. Pick only what your agent needs, because users see these on the consent screen.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

values.label: Installation scope
values.value: Any workspace (needed for a Marketplace listing) or Selected workspaces only

values.label: Capabilities
values.value: Read content / Update content / Insert content; User information: None, Without email, or With email

gotchas: Redirect URIs must include a protocol and can't contain fragments, relative paths, wildcards or a public IP address (per a community tutorial).
Without a user information capability, the list-users endpoint returns HTTP 403. Email addresses are only returned with 'With email'.

steps.title: Fill in company, website, privacy policy and terms details
steps.detail: An agent can draft a tagline, privacy policy and terms of use and check that the homepage, privacy and terms URLs load. You then enter them in the connection's distribution or organization settings. According to a community source, Notion shows these on the connection page and the authorization screens.
gotchas: Which of these fields are required wasn't confirmed from Notion's official form.

steps.title: Copy the OAuth client ID and client secret
steps.detail: Open the connection's Configuration tab and copy the OAuth client ID and OAuth client secret. Store the secret somewhere secure.
gotchas: Notion says the Authorization URL field on this tab only fills in after you submit for review. Composio doesn't need it, because it builds the authorize URL from your client ID.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config with your own credentials
steps.detail: In Composio, create a Notion (toolkit 'notion') OAuth2 auth config that uses your own credentials and paste in the client ID and secret. Leave scopes empty, because Notion doesn't use scope strings. Composio uses https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize with owner=user and exchanges the code at /v1/oauth/token using HTTP Basic auth.

values.label: Client ID
values.value: OAuth client ID from the Configuration tab

values.label: Client secret
values.value: OAuth client secret from the Configuration tab

gotchas: Make sure the redirect URI in Notion exactly matches Composio's callback URL. It is also sent in the token request.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a connection through Composio, approve the capabilities, and pick pages in the page picker. Then confirm that an API call such as a search returns those pages. If the install page fails, the connection may need to be submitted for review first (see step 8).
gotchas: The page picker only lists pages the user has full access to. The token can only reach the pages selected there.
Refreshing returns a new access token and a new refresh token, so always save the newest refresh token.

steps.title: Share the OAuth link with test users in other workspaces
steps.detail: Send test users your Composio connection link. Each user completes the flow and gets a token for their own workspace and the pages they choose. Every workspace member who needs access has to authorize separately.
gotchas: No documented install caps were found for unreviewed connections. Watch for errors as you add users.

steps.title: Submit the public connection for Notion security review
steps.detail: Submit the public connection for review from the Developer portal. Notion requires a security review before a connection can be listed, and the docs tie the Authorization URL field to this submission.
gotchas: What the security review checks and how long it takes are not documented in the sources found.

steps.title: Wait for the security review
steps.detail: Wait for Notion to finish the security review. No official timeline was found.

steps.title: Draft and submit a Marketplace listing
steps.detail: Under Listings > Connections, create a listing draft with a name, description, category, tags, logo and images, and link it to your public connection. An agent can draft the copy. You save it and click submit for review.
gotchas: Avoid Notion trademarks in your branding. Notion lists brand and trademark issues as a rejection reason, and links a Connection Gallery Best Practices guide.

steps.title: Wait for the listing review
steps.detail: Notion says to expect an email within 5-10 business days. If the listing is rejected, the email explains why; fix the issues and resubmit.

requirements.item: Public connection (not internal connection or personal access token)
requirements.detail: Only public connections use OAuth 2.0 and can be installed by other users.
Must include a protocol, with no fragments, wildcards, relative paths or public IPs. It is sent again in the token request.
Composio sets these. If you build your own flow, use both values every time.

requirements.item: Company website, privacy policy and terms URLs
requirements.detail: Shown on the connection page and authorization screens (community source; whether they're required is not confirmed).
Required for Marketplace eligibility and can only be set at creation.
Name, description, category, tags, logo and images, linked to the public connection.

scopes.effect: Lets the connection read pages and databases the user shared in the page picker. Notion uses capabilities instead of OAuth scope strings, so Composio's scope list stays empty.
Lets the connection edit existing content or create new content in shared pages. Users see these on the consent screen.
Needed for the users endpoints. Without any user capability, list-users returns 403.
Returns user email addresses. Whether it gets extra scrutiny in review is undocumented.

blockers.symptom: You need a Marketplace listing, but the connection is 'Selected workspaces only' (or an internal connection)
blockers.cause: Installation scope is fixed at creation, and only Any-workspace public connections can be listed.
blockers.fix: Create a new public connection with Any workspace scope and have users reconnect through it.

blockers.symptom: The Authorization URL field on the Configuration tab is empty, or the install page fails for your client ID
blockers.cause: Notion says the Authorization URL field only fills in after the public connection is submitted for review.
blockers.fix: Composio builds the authorize URL from your client ID, so test that first. If installs still fail, submit the connection for review.

blockers.cause: Brand or trademark issues, quality concerns, or not meeting baseline connection criteria.
blockers.fix: Fix the issues the email describes, following the Connection Gallery Best Practices guide, and resubmit.

blockers.symptom: HTTP 403 from the users endpoint, or no email addresses returned
blockers.cause: The connection was created without a user information capability, or without 'With email'.
blockers.fix: Enable the right user capability on the connection, then have users re-authorize.

composio.note: Composio's managed Notion app works right away, so start there for prototyping. Scopes are empty because Notion uses capabilities plus a per-user page picker. Register your own public connection if you want your own app name and branding on the consent screen, your own redirect URI, or a Marketplace listing. If you do, choose Any workspace scope from the start, and check that your connection can be authorized before review: Notion says the Authorization URL field only fills in after you submit for review.

evidence.quote: Public connections use OAuth 2.0 for authentication.

evidence.claim: A public connection is created in the Developer portal under Build > Public connections, with name, workspace, redirect URIs, installation scope and capabilities.
evidence.quote: In the Build section of the sidebar, select Public connections.

evidence.claim: Installation scope is set at creation and can't be changed afterward.
evidence.quote: Installation scope is set once, at creation time, and can't be changed afterward.

evidence.claim: The client ID and secret are on the connection's Configuration tab.

evidence.claim: The Authorization URL field only populates after the public connection is submitted for review.

evidence.claim: The authorize request takes client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, owner=user and an optional state.

evidence.claim: The code is exchanged at /v1/oauth/token using HTTP Basic auth with client_id and client_secret.
evidence.quote: The request is authorized using HTTP Basic Authentication.

evidence.claim: The token response includes access and refresh tokens; refreshing returns a new pair.
evidence.quote: Refreshing an access token will generate a new access token and a new refresh token.

evidence.claim: Each user must complete the authorization flow individually and gets a workspace-scoped token.
evidence.quote: each user needs to complete the authorization flow individually.

evidence.claim: Notion uses capabilities (content: read/update/insert; user info: none/without email/with email) instead of OAuth scope strings.
evidence.quote: Read content: This capability gives a connection access to read existing content in a Notion workspace.

evidence.claim: Calling list-users without user information capabilities returns 403; emails require the with-email capability.
evidence.quote: Attempting to call this API without user information capabilities will return an HTTP response with a 403 status code.

evidence.claim: Users pick pages in a page picker that only shows pages they have full access to.
evidence.quote: The page picker only displays pages or databases to which a user has full access

open_questions: Can users authorize a public connection before it is submitted for review? Notion says the Authorization URL field only fills in after submission, which may mean unreviewed connections can't be installed.
What the security review checks, what documents it needs and how long it takes, as distinct from the 5-10 business day listing review.
Whether there are rate limits or install caps for unreviewed or unlisted public connections.
Whether creating a public connection requires a paid plan, workspace-owner role, or business verification.
Exactly which fields are required for a public connection versus a Marketplace listing (privacy policy, terms, logo, demo video).
Whether the REST public-connection flow supports PKCE (only the hosted MCP server is reported to use it).
